item.title: Groups and Dynamics: Topology, Measure, and Borel Structure
item.description:
Authors: David Kerr, Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob, Tianyi Zheng

Source: Oberwolfach Reports

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Over the last couple of decades a major branch of study in groups and dynamics has blossomed around the basic structural themes of measure, topology, and Borelness. While several different currents of research have come to shape this theory, the picture that has emerged is one of a constellation of ideas and methods that cut across all three categories in an often surprisingly coordinated way, with constantly expanding connections to probability and geometric group theory. The workshop aimed to further advance this picture with a focus on a number of topics including hyperfiniteness, ergodic theorems, subgroup dynamics, random walks and the Poisson boundary, percolation, entropy, rigidity, Borel complexity, and genericity and classification in spaces of actions.

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Abstract: Human-facing AI systems are mainly designed and evaluated for what they do for users, and seldom for what sustained use does to users' own capabilities.
